title: Cabbage: modeled ₹882/qtl left, Kondotty → Chala
summary: January 2022: reported cabbage prices at Kondotty and Chala imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 83% of 12 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹882 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 944 same-variety market pairs screened for cabbage in January 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Chala report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2022
scenes.caption: Kondotty (Kerala) and Chala (Kerala) both reported cabbage prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 12 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kondotty reported a median ₹3,500 per quintal. Chala reported a median ₹5,026 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,626/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,626 per quintal, and Chala was dearer on 92% of days.

scenes.headline: 378 km by road
scenes.caption: 378 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~6 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹81/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹999 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹726 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Chala report, the rule selects 12 of 12 modeled shipping days. 10 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹882 per quintal (₹603 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Cabbage route from Kondotty to Chala was positive on 83% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹88,200, or ₹60,300 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to cabbage
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹81/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Cabbage route from Kondotty to Chala was positive on 83% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹88,200, or ₹60,300 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Cabbage: modeled ₹278/qtl left, Kangra (Baijnath) → Kullu
summary: December 2022: reported cabbage prices at Kangra (Baijnath) and Kullu imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 81% of 26 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹278 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 1,302 same-variety market pairs screened for cabbage in December 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kullu report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: December 2022
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) and Kullu (Himachal Pradesh) both reported cabbage prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 26 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹1,000 per quintal. Kullu reported a median ₹1,400 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹400/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹400 per quintal, and Kullu was dearer on 92% of days.

scenes.headline: 187 km by road
scenes.caption: 187 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹40/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹218 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹132 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kullu report, the rule selects 22 of 26 modeled shipping days. 21 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹278 per quintal (₹195 under stress).

scenes.caption: The modeled Cabbage route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Kullu was positive on 81% of matched days in December 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹27,800, or ₹19,500 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
